title_suffix: living feature docs, documentation obligations, and a smaller core
summary:
OSpec 2.0.0 replaces generated per-change knowledge documents with a living documentation layer — human-owned feature docs with declared `code:` scopes, a one-row-per-feature catalogue, a section-level locator, and a documentation-obligation engine that tells the AI exactly which section each change owes — and removes the plugin system, `ospec batch`, and a batch of dead library surface.

## Breaking changes

- **Plugin system removed.** The stitch and checkpoint built-ins, `ospec plugins`, and the third-party extension mechanism are gone. `ospec update` strips plugin configuration from `.skillrc` and managed guidance into an auditable `.ospec/plugin-migration.json`; `.ospec/plugins/` is user data and is never touched. Older 1.x CLIs that fetch the plugin registry from this repository now receive 404.
- **Archived changes no longer generate knowledge documents.** Nothing is written under `docs/project/changes/`; archiving writes the index entry, updates `docs/project/feature-catalog.md` rows, and maintains an idempotent `ospec:last-change` traceability comment. Render any archive on demand with `ospec changes show <archive>`. Projects with legacy generated documents migrate with the four-phase, gated `ospec docs migrate`.
- **`feature-index.md` is replaced by `feature-catalog.md`.** The prose blocks stop being generated; the catalogue carries one row per declared feature.
- **CLI surface**: `ospec batch` (with `stats`/`export`/`import`) is removed, and the always-failing 1.9 tombstones `ospec execute orchestrate`, `ospec workflow simulate`, and `ospec loop watch` are deleted outright.
- **Library surface**: 25 package-root exports are removed (including `BatchOperations`, `CachingLayer`, `FeatureUpdater`, `HookSystem`, `IndexRegenerator`, `PerformanceMonitor`, `SkillUpdateEngine`, `StatePersistence`, `VerificationSystem`, `WorkflowEngine`, `AgentCliRunnerService`, `BatchCommand`, `StringUtils`, `DateUtils` and their singletons), 15 type exports leave the package root, 16 deep `dist/**` import paths are deleted (including the whole `dist/advanced` subtree), and 29 members are removed from modules that still ship — most notably `TemplateEngine`'s eight `generate*Template` methods and `TaskGraphExecutionService.launchAndRun`/`orchestrate`/`runReview`. Importing the package as a library no longer auto-executes the CLI.
- **Task graphs from before contract 1.8.6**: a task without `parallelizable` is treated as serial, and serial-task mutual exclusion is now actually enforced — an unmarked `IN_PROGRESS` task defers other ready tasks (`scheduling.deferred` reason `serial_task_running:<id>`). Add `parallelizable: true` to genuinely independent tasks or regenerate the graph.
- **Index ordering** switches from locale-dependent `localeCompare` to fixed codepoint order: the first `ospec index build` after upgrading re-sorts the index once, and collaborators stop producing byte-different indexes across locales.
- **Verification evidence** accepts negative exit codes and records `timedOut`/`signal`/`infraFailure` as independent fields.

## Migration

1. `npm install -g @clawplays/ospec-cli@2.0.0`
2. In each project: `ospec update` — refreshes assets, repairs legacy footprints, strips plugin configuration with an audit record, and reports legacy generated documents without touching them.
3. `ospec index build` — applies the one-time codepoint re-sort.
4. When ready, `ospec docs migrate --plan` starts the guided migration from generated documents to feature docs; nothing is deleted until phase 3 verifies every document is mapped or explicitly marked historical.
new: Living feature docs: declare a feature section with `<!-- ospec:feature <slug> code:<paths> -->` inside human-owned docs; `docs/project/feature-catalog.md` carries one row per declared feature (slug, one line, `doc#section`, status, last-change archive).

`ospec docs locate --feature <slug> | --affects <path>`: resolves the ONE section that describes a behavior — path, heading, and line range — through the `code:` declarations, longest prefix first, so an agent reads one section instead of a document.

Documentation-obligation engine: `ospec docs obligations --apply` derives per-`change_type` obligations at planning time with the resolved `path#section` already filled in (a fix checks the section for the pre-fix wrong behaviour; a refactor verifies it and can record `verified_unchanged` via `ospec docs confirm`). When `features:` is empty, obligations fall back to resolving `affects` through the `code:` declarations. `.skillrc` `docs_contract.mode: warn|strict` decides whether an unmet required obligation warns or blocks archiving; the default is `warn` for this release cycle.
`ospec docs audit`: read-only drift detection — lists feature sections whose `code:` paths changed since the archive named by their `ospec:last-change` comment.

`ospec changes show <archive>`: renders an archived change (summary, affects, file list, verification commands, evidence links) from the index and archive directory; fuzzy name matching offers candidates.

`ospec docs migrate`: four-phase migration for pre-2.0 projects — plan (inventory + draft skeletons), rewrite (AI work, the engine never writes prose), verify (refuses to proceed while any legacy document is unmapped), finalize (deletes only after printing and recording the list).
`ospec index gc`: lists index entries whose archive no longer exists and cleans them on confirmation.

Controller batch protocol: `ospec loop step --batch-file` settles a whole action batch in one round trip (controller round trips drop from 7 to 2 per cycle), and structured worker reports validate at completion time.

Forward-compatible config: a `.skillrc` declaring a schema version this CLI does not know has its unknown `workflow` keys tolerated, preserved through save round-trips, and warned about once — while a known-version config still fails loud on typos.
improved: `ospec archive --check` and `ospec execute status` are truly read-only: they no longer take the task-graph mutation lease or rewrite state; `--repair` restores the old reconciling behaviour explicitly, and goal-progress coordination diagnostics are still reported read-only.

Command output is budgeted: prose output over the cap spills the complete text to `artifacts/spill/` and references it inline; machine output (`--json`/`--brief`) is never truncated — over the cap it is replaced by one valid JSON envelope with `ospecOutputSpill: true`.

`ospec update` migrates legacy plugin configuration safely, repairs older project footprints, refreshes managed skills and archive layout, and points at `ospec docs migrate` when it finds legacy generated documents — it never migrates or deletes them itself.
Serial-task scheduling is enforced correctly under concurrency, state files use compare-and-swap and atomic writes, and repeated repair findings stop instead of cycling.
fixed: Verification and review-evidence validation always derives from the bytes actually read — the caching layer that could return a stale PASS after a file changed mid-validation was removed entirely.
`ospec index query` matches project documents, not only archived changes.
A damaged `.skillrc` fails loud with recovery steps everywhere (25 call sites no longer silently fall back to the classic layout), and checklist gates handle CRLF content instead of failing open.
`--help`, `-h`, and a leading `help` print help and never act: previously 11 subcommands swallowed them as positional arguments, and `ospec goal help` really created 18 files.
Unreadable archives keep their index entries and warn instead of being silently dropped, and `runGit` no longer truncates large git evidence at 1MB.
docs: READMEs in all four languages present the 2.0 documentation layer; usage pages list the new `docs`, `changes show`, and `index gc` commands; every reference to removed features (plugin system, `ospec batch`, generated knowledge documents, tombstone commands) is gone from the shipped docs and protocol assets.
